evidence.title: Jules FAQ
evidence.locator: Leave while working; Failure handling; Training; Free access
evidence.finding: Jules can work after the user leaves the app, notifies plan/task completion, retries failed steps and never trains on private repository content. A recurring no-cost plan is documented. Setup scripts do not support long-lived servers.

evidence.title: Jules Limits and Plans
evidence.finding: Free, Pro and Ultra document daily limits of 15/100/300 and concurrent limits of 3/15/60. Paid Google AI plans require individual Gmail accounts; business/Workspace upgrade routes are not yet available.

evidence.title: Jules Environment setup
evidence.finding: Repository setup scripts install dependencies and run discrete checks. Successful Run and Snapshot captures the environment for future tasks, including preinstalled runtimes and tools.

evidence.title: Reviewing Jules code
evidence.finding: Jules exposes activity/errors, per-file and expanded diffs, real-time feedback, downloadable changes and a completion summary with runtime, files, lines and branch/commit details. Publish branch/PR controls export changes.

evidence.title: Jules REST API
evidence.finding: Alpha REST API uses X-Goog-Api-Key, with up to three keys. Sessions and activities expose plans, messages and progress. Alpha specifications and keys may change.

evidence.title: Repoless, outputs and activity filters
evidence.finding: REST API can start sessions without a repository and return changed-file outputs in Git patch format. Activities are immutable records with timestamp filters and can reconstruct a session.

evidence.title: Jules Planning
evidence.finding: Jules creates a step plan after setup and revises it from chat feedback. Approve plan starts execution, but the documentation says a timer may auto-approve when the user leaves.

evidence.title: Jules Errors and failures
evidence.finding: Failed steps are retried where possible, including network/install faults. Persistent failures get a failed state and UI badge. Humans can change setup/prompt and rerun.

evidence.title: Jules gains memory
evidence.finding: Jules saves preferences, nudges and corrections during a task and references them in later same-repository tasks. Memory can be toggled per repository under Knowledge in repo settings.

evidence.title: Jules CI Fixer and authorship
evidence.finding: Jules receives failed GitHub Actions checks on its own PRs, fixes and resubmits. User-level settings choose Jules-only, coauthored or user-only commits.

evidence.title: Update Scheduled Tasks
evidence.finding: The dated release adds schedule editing, pause and resume without deleting and recreating the task; the undated schedule guide still says editing is unavailable.

evidence.title: Jules web-app testing
evidence.finding: Jules can render and verify a frontend, returning a screenshot with the code changes. The base image includes Playwright.

evidence.title: Google Terms linked from Jules
evidence.locator: Jules homepage Terms of Service link; Google service/software permissions and intellectual property
evidence.finding: The Jules homepage links Google Terms of Service for its hosted application. These are vendor-authored service/software terms retaining Google intellectual-property rights, not an open-source grant for the hosted coding agent. Public SDK or example repositories do not establish the core service license.

evidence.title: Jules Tools remote-session architecture
evidence.finding: Jules Tools is a local npm CLI/TUI for Google-authenticated remote sessions. It controls the Google-hosted Jules worker rather than executing the coding agent on the client or a user server.

evidence.title: Jules API resource scope
evidence.finding: The documented primary API resources are sources, sessions and session activities. This establishes a session/run API, but not independent issue-backlog records, human workspace roles or a shared-human prompting model.

evidence.title: Jules Getting started
evidence.locator: Login; Connect GitHub; Starting your first task; Include AGENTS.md file; Enabling notifications
evidence.finding: Users sign in with a Google account, connect GitHub and choose repositories, pick a repo and branch, write a prompt and request a plan to approve. Jules reads AGENTS.md at the repository root. Browser notifications report completion or a need for input.

evidence.title: Running Tasks with Jules
evidence.locator: Choose a repo and branch; Write a clear prompt; Attach visual context; Watching Jules work; Final summary; Giving feedback mid-task; Pausing Jules; Starting tasks from GitHub Issues
evidence.finding: Tasks start from a plain-language prompt in the web prompt box on a chosen repo and branch, with optional PNG/JPEG images (under 5 MB) that are never committed. An activity feed, mini diffs and a diff editor show progress; chat feedback mid-task makes Jules replan. Tasks can be paused. Adding the jules label to a GitHub issue starts a task; Jules comments on the issue and links the resulting pull request.

evidence.title: Managing tasks and repos
evidence.locator: Starting tasks; Pausing or deleting tasks; Managing repositories
evidence.finding: Several tasks can run simultaneously, each in its own VM with its own logs, environment setup and code changes. Paused tasks can be resumed; deleted tasks are removed permanently. Jules can only access GitHub repositories the user explicitly allows; other version control systems are future work.

evidence.title: Jules Repo view
evidence.finding: The repo view lists running tasks first, completed tasks with full logs and diffs, and clearly labelled failed or waiting tasks; any task can be reopened to review its plan or continue feedback.

evidence.title: Jules Limits and Plans
evidence.locator: Plan Availability note; Plan Comparison; FAQ
evidence.finding: Plans allow 15/100/300 tasks per rolling 24 hours and 3/15/60 concurrent tasks (Jules, Pro, Ultra), all with Gemini models. Paid plans come with Google AI Pro/Ultra and are only for individual @gmail.com accounts; business users fill an interest form. Family plan members each get their own limits. Users must be 18 or older. At the daily limit new tasks are blocked while existing tasks remain accessible.

evidence.title: Jules FAQ
evidence.locator: What is Jules?; Is Jules available without cost?; How does Jules work under the hood?; security; Can I leave Jules while its working?; What happens if a task fails?; Does Jules train on private repos?
evidence.finding: Jules is in Public Beta and includes a no-cost plan. Each task runs in a fresh cloud VM with internet access where Jules clones the repo and installs dependencies. Users can leave the app after submitting a task. Failed tasks are retried automatically, then marked failed with a notification.

evidence.title: Jules Environment setup
evidence.locator: intro; Add a setup script; Test your setup script; Environment Snapshots
evidence.finding: Each task runs in a secure, short-lived Ubuntu VM. Without a script Jules studies the repository and uses AGENTS.md or README.md for setup hints; setup scripts can be validated with Run and Snapshot, and the snapshot is reused by later tasks in that repository.

evidence.title: Reviewing code changes
evidence.locator: Activity feed; Code diffs; Interactive feedback; Task summary; Pushing to GitHub
evidence.finding: A real-time activity feed logs steps, outputs, errors and requests for feedback; the diff editor shows all changed files with download and copy. Publish branch or Publish PR pushes to GitHub, after which users review and merge the PR themselves.

evidence.title: Reviewing plans & giving feedback
evidence.finding: Jules presents a step-by-step plan for approval; feedback in chat makes it update the plan. If the user navigates away, the plan is auto-approved on a timer.

evidence.title: Jules Errors and failures
evidence.locator: How errors are reported; Automatic retry behavior; Debugging environment setup
evidence.finding: Errors appear in the activity feed and as a red notification badge; transient failures are retried, persistent ones mark the task failed; users can rerun from the task summary after editing the setup script or prompt.

evidence.title: Jules Feedback and support
evidence.locator: Giving feedback in the UI; What happens after you submit feedback
evidence.finding: Feedback goes through an in-app form; the team will not reply to every submission.

evidence.title: Jules Contact
evidence.finding: Questions and support go through the Google Labs Discord or X.

evidence.title: Jules Suggested Tasks
evidence.locator: Enabling Suggested Tasks; Reviewing and Running Suggestions; Feedback and Dismissal
evidence.finding: Proactivity scans up to five repositories for resolvable #TODO comments; suggestion cards can be started with Start or dismissed.

evidence.title: Jules Scheduled Tasks
evidence.locator: Creating a Scheduled Task; Managing Scheduled Tasks; Common Use Cases
evidence.finding: Recurring tasks run automatically at a set frequency and cadence; three templated scheduled tasks (performance, design, security) are offered. The page says editing a scheduled task is not supported.

evidence.title: Jules Integrations
evidence.finding: Integrations are read-only by default, can trigger Jules from external events, and store API keys encrypted, never exposed in chat or shared between sessions.

evidence.title: Jules REST API Quickstart

evidence.finding: The alpha REST API uses Jules API keys (at most 3) in X-Goog-Api-Key. Sessions have stable IDs; automationMode AUTO_CREATE_PR is optional (default no PR); API sessions auto-approve plans unless requirePlanApproval is true.

evidence.title: Jules REST API Sessions

evidence.finding: Sessions can be created, listed, read, deleted, messaged and have plans approved; states are QUEUED, PLANNING, AWAITING_PLAN_APPROVAL, AWAITING_USER_FEEDBACK, IN_PROGRESS, PAUSED, COMPLETED and FAILED.

evidence.title: Jules Tools Reference

evidence.finding: Jules Tools installs from npm, signs in with the Google account, lists repositories and remote sessions, starts sessions (optionally several in parallel) and pulls results; the TUI shows sessions and diffs.

evidence.title: Jules changelog: Jules Turndown
evidence.finding: Jules winds down on 2026-12-31; sessions could continue until 2026-11-11, after which Jules is read-only. evidence.title: Jules changelog: Planning Critic
